Main Characters الشخصيات الرئيسية

Santiago سانتياغو

الصياد العجوز
  • Santiago is a brave old fisherman who never gives up easily.سانتياغو هو صياد عجوز شجاع لا يستسلم بسهولة.
  • He is patient and determined when facing difficulties.يتميز بالصبر والإصرار فى مواجهة الصعوبات.
  • He respects the sea and the fish even though he hunts it.يحترم البحر والسمكة رغم أنه يصطادها.
  • He believes in hope and never loses confidence in himself.يؤمن بالأمل ولا يفقد ثقته بنفسه.
  • He has dignity and depends on himself.يتمتع بالكرامة ويعتمد على نفسه.
  • We learn patience, courage, and perseverance from him.نتعلم منه الصبر والشجاعة والمثابرة.

Manolin مانولين

الصبى المخلص
  • Manolin is a loyal boy who loves Santiago very much.مانولين صبى مخلص يحب سانتياغو كثيرًا.
  • He always cares for and looks after him.يهتم به ويعتنى به دائمًا.
  • He trusts Santiago's experience and respects him.يثق بخبرة سانتياغو ويحترمه.
  • He represents hope and support in Santiago's life.يمثل الأمل والدعم فى حياة سانتياغو.
  • We learn loyalty and respect from him.نتعلم منه الوفاء والاحترام.

The Marlin سمكة المارلين

الخصم العظيم
  • The marlin is a strong and great fish.المارلين سمكة قوية وعظيمة.
  • It represents Santiago's greatest challenge.تمثل التحدى الحقيقى لسانتياغو.
  • Santiago respected it and called it his brother.احترمه سانتياغو وناداه أخاه.
  • It symbolizes strength and beauty.ترمز إلى القوة والجمال.

The Sharks أسماك القرش

رمز الخسارة
  • The sharks represent difficulty and loss.تمثل أسماك القرش الصعوبات والخسائر.
  • They destroyed the result of Santiago's hard work.دمرت ثمرة تعب سانتياغو.

Success and Failure النجاح والفشل

The Moral العبرة من القصة

The Summary الملخص الكامل

The story is about Santiago, an old Cuban fisherman. He is poor and has been unlucky, because he has not caught a fish for eighty-four days. Many people think he is finished, but he is still strong in spirit. His only true friend is Manolin, a young boy who once fished with him. The boy's parents do not allow him to go with Santiago anymore, but he still helps the old man with food and care.

القصة عن سانتياغو، صياد كوبى عجوز. فقير وغير محظوظ لأنه لم يصطد سمكة لمدة أربعة وثمانين يومًا. كثير من الناس يظنون أنه انتهى، لكنه ما زال قويًا فى روحه. صديقه الحقيقى الوحيد هو مانولين، فتى صغير كان يصطاد معه. والدا الفتى لا يسمحان له بالذهاب مع سانتياغو، لكنه ما زال يساعد الرجل العجوز بالطعام والرعاية.

One day, Santiago goes alone into the sea, determined to prove himself. He sails far out into the Gulf Stream and finally hooks a giant marlin, the biggest fish he has ever seen. The fish is powerful, and Santiago cannot pull it in. Instead, the marlin pulls the boat for two days and nights. Santiago suffers from hunger, pain, and weakness, but he never gives up. He admires the marlin's strength and beauty and respects it as a worthy opponent.

وذات يوم، يخرج سانتياغو وحيدًا إلى البحر، عازمًا على أن يبرهن على قوته. يبحر بعيدًا فى تيار الخليج، وأخيرًا يصطاد سمكة مارلين عملاقة، أكبر سمكة رآها فى حياته. السمكة قوية، وسانتياغو لا يستطيع سحبها. بدلًا من ذلك، السمكة هى التى تسحب القارب يومين وليلتين. يعانى سانتياغو من الجوع والألم والضعف، لكنه لا يستسلم أبدًا. يعجب بقوة السمكة وجمالها ويحترمها كخصم يستحق التقدير.

At last, Santiago manages to kill the marlin with his harpoon. He ties it to his boat and begins the journey home. He feels proud of his victory and dreams of how people will admire the great fish.

أخيرًا يتمكن سانتياغو من قتل المارلين برمحه. يربطها فى قاربه ويبدأ رحلة العودة إلى البيت. يشعر بالفخر بانتصاره ويحلم كيف سيُعجب الناس بالسمكة الكبيرة.

On his way back, however, sharks attack the marlin. They smell its blood in the water and come in groups. Santiago fights them bravely with his harpoon, an oar, and even a knife tied to a stick. He kills many sharks, but more and more arrive. In the end, they eat almost all of the marlin, leaving only its skeleton.

فى طريق عودته، تهاجم أسماك القرش سمكة المارلين. تشم دمها فى الماء وتأتى فى جماعات. يقاتل سانتياغو أسماك القرش بشجاعة مستخدمًا رمحه ومجدافًا وحتى سكينًا مربوطًا فى عصا. يقتل الكثير من القروش، لكن المزيد والمزيد منها يأتى. فى النهاية، تأكل القروش تقريبًا كل السمكة، ولم يبق سوى هيكلها العظمى.

Santiago reaches the shore completely exhausted. He has lost the meat of the marlin, but he has not lost his pride or dignity. The people in the village are amazed when they see the huge skeleton tied to his boat. They realize that Santiago is still a great fisherman.

يصل سانتياغو إلى الشاطئ مرهقًا تمامًا. لقد خسر لحم المارلين، لكنه لم يخسر كبرياءه أو كرامته. يندهش الناس فى القرية عندما يرون الهيكل العظمى الضخم مربوطًا فى قاربه. ويدركون أن سانتياغو ما زال صيادًا عظيمًا.

The boy Manolin promises to fish with Santiago again and take care of him. Santiago, tired but peaceful, dreams of lions on the beaches of Africa, symbols of his youth, hope, and eternal strength.

يعد مانولين أن يصطاد مع سانتياغو مرة أخرى وأن يهتم به. أما سانتياغو، المتعب ولكن الهادئ، فيحلم بالأسود على شواطئ إفريقيا، رمزًا لشبابه وأمله وقوته الأبدية.

📝 Summary الملخص

Santiago was an old Cuban fisherman who had gone eighty-four days without catching a fish. Although people in the village thought he was unlucky, he remained proud and determined. Only Manolin, a young boy, stayed loyal to him and respected him deeply. Manolin helped Santiago with his fishing tools and believed that his luck would return. Santiago lived in a simple hut and never complained about his poor life. He shared a meal with the boy and talked about his love for baseball and Joe DiMaggio. Santiago admired DiMaggio because he played despite pain and never gave up. The old man believed that fishing needed skill, patience, and courage, not only luck. He planned to go far into the sea on the eighty-fifth day to catch a great fish. Santiago remembered his youth, his voyages to Africa, and his dreams of lions. The lions represented his strength, freedom, and hope. Before sleeping, Santiago believed that his luck was about to change.

كان سانتياغو صيادًا كوبيًا عجوزًا لم يصطد أى سمكة لمدة أربعة وثمانين يومًا. ورغم أن أهل القرية اعتبروه سيئ الحظ، ظل فخورًا ومصممًا. كان مانولين، الصبى الصغير، هو الشخص الوحيد الذى ظل مخلصًا له ويحترمه بشدة. كان مانولين يساعد سانتياغو فى أدوات الصيد ويؤمن أن حظه سيعود. عاش سانتياغو فى كوخ بسيط ولم يشتكِ أبدًا من فقر حياته. تناول وجبة مع الصبى وتحدث عن حبه للبيسبول واللاعب جو ديماجيو. كان سانتياغو معجبًا بديماجيو لأنه كان يلعب رغم الألم ولم يستسلم. وكان يؤمن بأن الصيد يحتاج إلى المهارة والصبر والشجاعة وليس الحظ فقط. خطط للذهاب بعيدًا فى البحر فى اليوم الخامس والثمانين ليصطاد سمكة كبيرة. تذكر شبابه ورحلاته إلى إفريقيا وأحلامه بالأسود. كانت الأسود ترمز إلى قوته وحريته وأمله. وقبل أن ينام، آمن سانتياغو بأن حظه سيتغير قريبًا.

📖 The Text النص

0 / 0

Santiago was an old fisherman, and the sea was his companion. His skin had grown dark and leathery from years beneath the burning sun. His hands were rough, cut, and scarred from pulling heavy fishing lines day after day. Yet, when people looked into his eyes, they did not see weakness. His eyes were as clear and bright as the sea itself, full of life and determination. For eighty-four long days, Santiago had gone out into the Gulf Stream and returned empty-handed. Not a single fish had been caught. In his small Cuban village, whispers began to spread. The younger fishermen, who still had luck, laughed at him quietly. They called him salao—the worst kind of unlucky.

Yet Santiago carried himself with dignity. He walked proudly with his fishing gear over his shoulder, his back straight, as if luck were something that could never truly defeat a man. Among all the people of the village, only one remained loyal to him: a boy named Manolin. The boy had fished with Santiago since he was just five years old. Now he was twelve, strong and full of admiration for the old man. He loved Santiago like a grandfather. For forty days, Manolin had fished with him, even when there was no catch. But finally, at his parents' order, he had joined another boat—a luckier boat that brought back fish.

Still, every evening, when the other fishermen returned with their catch, Manolin would go to Santiago's small skiff. He would help the old man carry his nets, his gaff, and his harpoon. He would fold the patched sail. He would carry the old man's heavy lines, carefully coiled, and walk beside him.

"Old man," the boy said one evening as they reached Santiago's hut, "you are the greatest fisherman I know. Someday, the luck will return to you."

Santiago smiled faintly, the lines of age deepening around his mouth.

"It is better to be lucky," he said. "But I would rather be exact. When luck finally comes, I want to be ready for it."

The boy nodded. He knew Santiago's words carried wisdom. To fish was not only luck—it was skill, patience, and courage. The hut where Santiago lived was small, made of faded palm leaves. Inside, it was almost bare. On the walls hung only two pictures. There was a bed made of newspapers, a single blanket, a wooden table, and one chair. There were no luxuries, no decorations, no treasures—except the tools of a fisherman. Yet Santiago never complained. He had lived his whole life with the sea, and that was enough. That evening, the boy sat with him outside the hut. They shared a simple meal of black beans, rice, and a little fried fish.

The boy had brought it as a gift from his own home. Santiago ate slowly, gratefully, for food was energy, and tomorrow he would need it.

"Tell me about baseball," Santiago said suddenly. Baseball was one of the old man's greatest loves. "How are the Yankees playing this season?"

"The Yankees are strong," Manolin replied eagerly. "Joe DiMaggio is playing well. He is always the hero."

Santiago's eyes lit up. "Yes, DiMaggio. He is my champion too. He played even when he had pain in his heel, yet he never gave up. That is real courage. Pain does not matter to a man."

The boy grinned. "But you are stronger than DiMaggio, old man. You have the sea."

The old man laughed, a soft, tired laugh. "Perhaps. But baseball has its battles, and the sea has its own." The evening grew darker. A warm breeze carried the smell of salt from the sea. The sound of waves reached their ears, steady and calming. Santiago leaned back against the wall of his hut, his face peaceful.

"Tomorrow is the eighty-fifth day," he said. "That is a lucky number. I will go far out, farther than the others dare to go. Maybe too far. But I must find the big fish."

The boy looked at him with admiration. "I wish I could go with you."

"You have your boat," Santiago said gently. "But you are always with me in spirit."

For a moment, silence fell between them. Santiago's thoughts drifted back to his youth. He had once been strong, a sailor on great ships. He had traveled to Africa, and on the golden beaches at night he had seen lions—young lions running and playing like children. Those lions had never left his mind. Even now, in his old age, he dreamed of them. They reminded him of strength, youth, and freedom.

"Do you know what I dream of, boy?" Santiago asked softly.

"Yes," said Manolin. "You dream of lions."

The old man smiled. "Yes, lions. Always the lions."

When the meal was finished, Manolin cleared the dishes and promised to bring food again tomorrow. Then he left for his parents' house. Santiago watched him go, feeling both proud and lonely. The boy had strength and future; the old man had only the sea. Later, Santiago lay down on his bed of newspapers. The hut was dark, but the sound of the ocean filled the silence. He thought of the coming day, of the deep waters, of the great fish that waited for him. He thought of Joe DiMaggio, who played through pain, and of the lions, who never feared. Slowly, he closed his eyes. Sleep came to him gently, and with it, the dream of lions. In his dream, they played freely on the beaches of Africa, their golden bodies shining in the sun. Santiago was young again, strong, fearless, full of hope. And as he dreamed, the old man smiled. Tomorrow would be the eighty-fifth day. His luck, he believed, was about to change.

1Why did the villagers think Santiago was unlucky?

✍️ General Exercises تدريبات عامة — بنماذج إجابة

1Why does Santiago admire Joe DiMaggio?
لماذا يعجب سانتياغو بـ جو ديماجيو؟
Because DiMaggio played through the pain in his heel and never gave up; he is a symbol of real courage.
لأن ديماجيو لعب رغم الألم فى كعبه ولم يستسلم؛ فهو رمز للشجاعة الحقيقية.
2How do the lions in Santiago's dreams symbolize youth and strength?
كيف ترمز الأسود فى أحلام سانتياغو إلى الشباب والقوة؟
He saw them as a young sailor in Africa; they play freely and fearlessly, so they remind him of the strength and freedom he had when he was young.
رآها وهو بحّار شاب فى إفريقيا؛ تلعب بحرية وبلا خوف، فتذكّره بالقوة والحرية التى كان يملكها فى شبابه.
3Why does Hemingway show the boy's loyalty, even when he fishes on another boat?
لماذا يُظهر همنجواى وفاء الصبى حتى وهو يصطاد على قارب آخر؟
To show that true loyalty and love are not controlled by luck or orders; the boy obeys his parents but still cares for the old man every evening.
ليبين أن الوفاء والحب الحقيقيين لا يحكمهما الحظ ولا الأوامر؛ الصبى يطيع والديه لكنه يعتنى بالعجوز كل مساء.
4What role does baseball play in the old man's life?
ما دور البيسبول فى حياة العجوز؟
It is one of his greatest loves; talking about it gives him hope, joy and motivation.
هو أحد أعظم أحبّائه؛ الحديث عنه يمنحه الأمل والبهجة والدافع.
5How does Santiago's preparation show the value of patience and skill?
كيف يُظهر استعداد سانتياغو قيمة الصبر والمهارة؟
He keeps his lines carefully coiled and plans to be exact, because he believes that when luck comes he must be ready for it.
يحفظ خيوطه ملفوفة بعناية ويخطط ليكون دقيقًا، لأنه يؤمن أنه عندما يأتى الحظ يجب أن يكون مستعدًا له.
6Why does Santiago dream of lions instead of fish? العمرانية ٢٠٣٦
لماذا يحلم سانتياغو بالأسود بدلًا من الأسماك؟
Fish are his daily work, but the lions are memories of youth, strength and freedom that fill him with hope.
الأسماك عمله اليومى، أما الأسود فهى ذكريات الشباب والقوة والحرية التى تملؤه بالأمل.
7In what way does Santiago's hut reflect his personality?
كيف يعكس كوخ سانتياغو شخصيته؟
It is small and bare with only a bed, a table, a chair and two pictures. It shows that he is poor, simple and humble, but proud and satisfied with the sea.
صغير وخالٍ إلا من سرير ومنضدة وكرسى وصورتين. يبين أنه فقير وبسيط ومتواضع، لكنه فخور وراضٍ بالبحر.
8Do you think luck or skill is more important for success? Why?
هل تعتقد أن الحظ أم المهارة أهم للنجاح؟ ولماذا؟
Skill is more important, as Santiago says: it is better to be exact. Luck may come or go, but skill, patience and preparation make a person ready to use any chance.
المهارة أهم كما يقول سانتياغو: الأفضل أن تكون دقيقًا. الحظ قد يأتى أو يذهب، لكن المهارة والصبر والاستعداد تجعل الإنسان جاهزًا لاستغلال أى فرصة.
9How did Manolin show loyalty to Santiago even after leaving his boat?
كيف أظهر مانولين وفاءه لسانتياغو حتى بعد أن ترك قاربه؟
Every evening he helped him carry his nets and harpoon, folded his sail, brought him food from his own home and encouraged him.
كل مساء كان يساعده فى حمل الشباك والرمح، ويطوى شراعه، ويحضر له الطعام من بيته، ويشجعه.
10What lesson can we learn about perseverance from this chapter?
ما الدرس الذى نتعلمه عن المثابرة من هذا الفصل؟
That we should never give up after failure. Santiago failed for 84 days, yet he kept his dignity and planned to go farther than anyone the next day.
ألا نستسلم أبدًا بعد الفشل. فشل سانتياغو ٨٤ يومًا، ومع ذلك حافظ على كرامته وخطط أن يذهب فى اليوم التالى أبعد من أى أحد.

📝 Summary ملخص الفصل

Santiago woke up early before sunrise and prepared for another day at sea. Manolin brought him food and helped him carry his fishing equipment to the harbor. Santiago thanked the boy but decided to fish alone because Manolin was working on another lucky boat. Santiago believed that the eighty-fifth day would bring him good fortune. Before leaving, Manolin wished him good luck and promised to help if he caught a big fish. Santiago rowed far beyond the other fishermen because he believed the biggest fish lived in deep waters. As he sailed, he remembered his youth, his adventures, and his dreams of Africa. When he reached a quiet place, he carefully prepared and lowered his fishing lines into the sea. He patiently waited, ignoring the small fish because he wanted to catch something extraordinary. The hot sun did not weaken his determination or his hope. Finally, he noticed a bird circling above the water and believed it was a sign that a great fish was nearby. Santiago remained calm, confident, and ready for the challenge ahead.

استيقظ سانتياجو مبكرًا قبل شروق الشمس واستعد ليوم جديد في البحر. أحضر له مانولين الطعام وساعده في حمل أدوات الصيد إلى الميناء. شكر سانتياجو الصبي، لكنه قرر أن يصطاد بمفرده لأن مانولين كان يعمل على قارب محظوظ آخر. كان سانتياجو يؤمن بأن اليوم الخامس والثمانين سيجلب له الحظ. قبل رحيله، تمنى له مانولين التوفيق ووعده بمساعدته إذا اصطاد سمكة كبيرة. أبحر سانتياجو بعيدًا عن بقية الصيادين لأنه كان يعتقد أن أكبر الأسماك تعيش في المياه العميقة. وأثناء الإبحار، تذكر شبابه ومغامراته وأحلامه عن أفريقيا. وعندما وصل إلى مكان هادئ، جهز خيوط الصيد بعناية وأنزلها في البحر. وانتظر بصبر، متجاهلًا الأسماك الصغيرة لأنه كان يبحث عن صيد استثنائي. ولم تضعف حرارة الشمس عزيمته أو أمله. وأخيرًا، لاحظ طائرًا يحلق فوق الماء، فاعتبر ذلك علامة على وجود سمكة كبيرة قريبة. وظل سانتياجو هادئًا وواثقًا ومستعدًا للتحدي القادم.

📖 The Text نص الفصل

0 / 0

In the early morning, before the sun rose, Santiago woke up. The sky was dark and full of stars. He loved this hour, when the village was quiet and the sea whispered in the distance. He put on his old trousers, picked up his coil of lines, and stepped outside his small hut. The boy, Manolin, was already waiting for him. He carried food wrapped in paper — a gift for Santiago.

"Here, old man. Some black beans, rice, and a little coffee," he said proudly.

Santiago accepted it gratefully.

"You are good to me, boy. I will need my strength today."

The boy helped him carry the lines, gaff, harpoon, and the sail, which was patched many times and looked like the flag of defeat. But Santiago carried it with pride, for he believed the sail would take him to his destiny.

As they walked toward the harbor, they passed other fishermen preparing their boats. Some greeted Santiago with respect, while others looked at him with pity. Santiago ignored both. He knew what he must do. They reached the small wooden skiff, Santiago's boat. It was old but seaworthy. The boy loaded the gear carefully, arranging the lines in neat coils so they would run freely when needed.

"Can I come with you?" Manolin asked.

"You are with a lucky boat now," Santiago replied. "Stay with them. I will manage alone. But when I catch the big one, you will help me carry it back."

The boy's eyes shone. "I believe in you, old man." They sat together for a moment on the dock, sipping the warm coffee from tin cups.

The air smelled of salt and tar, and the sea waited silently. Santiago looked at the horizon.

"Eighty-five is my number," he said. "Today, I will go far out. Farther than the others dare to go."

The boy nodded. "You always go too far." Santiago smiled. "That is where the big fish live."

When the stars began to fade and the first light of dawn touched the water, Santiago pushed his boat away from the shore. The boy held the rope for a moment, then let go.

"Good luck, old man," Manolin said softly.

"Good luck," Santiago answered, though he believed luck was only part of the story. Skill, patience, and endurance mattered more.

The boat moved smoothly over the calm water. Santiago rowed with steady arms, feeling the rhythm of the oars. He listened to the sounds of the sea: the splash of fish, the cries of seabirds, the gentle slap of waves. He felt at home. As he rowed, he thought about his life. He remembered when he was young and strong, when he had sailed to Africa and seen lions playing on the golden beaches. He remembered storms, battles with giant fish, and long nights on the open sea. He was old now, but his spirit was not broken.

By sunrise, he was far from the shore. He could no longer see the lights of the village. The sea stretched wide and endless around him. Other boats had stopped closer in, but Santiago kept going. He wanted to be alone where no one else dared to fish. At last, he stopped and prepared his lines.

He baited them carefully with fresh sardines and lowered them into the deep blue water, at different depths. He worked with the precision of a master, for he believed that exactness brought luck. Then he sat back, holding the line gently between his fingers, feeling every movement below. He waited, patient as always. The sun climbed higher, and the sea shone like glass. The old man thought of the boy and smiled.

"He has hope," Santiago whispered to himself. "It is good for a man to have hope. Without it, he is nothing."

All morning he waited. Small fish tugged at the bait, but he ignored them. He was looking for something greater, something worthy of all his strength. By noon, the heat was strong, and sweat ran down his back.

But Santiago did not complain. He kept his eyes on the sea, his hands ready, his heart steady. He was prepared for the great test. Far out, a bird circled over the water. Santiago watched it carefully.

"Where the bird circles, there are fish," he said aloud.

His eyes followed the movement, and deep inside, he knew that soon, his moment would come.

📝 Summary ملخص الفصل

The sun was high as Santiago watched a bird diving toward the sea, signaling the presence of fish. Soon, he felt a powerful fish slowly take the bait. Santiago stayed calm and allowed the fish to swallow it completely before pulling the line. The giant fish was hooked and began towing the boat far into the open sea. Santiago admired the fish's great strength and refused to give up. He drank water and ate a little tuna to keep his energy. As night fell, the fish continued pulling the boat without stopping. The fishing line injured Santiago's hands, and his back and arms became painful, but he remained determined. He thought of Joe DiMaggio and encouraged himself to endure pain with courage. Santiago wished Manolin were with him to help and witness the great battle. Although he was completely alone, he felt connected to the sea and nature. At dawn, the fish was still strong, and Santiago accepted that the struggle would continue until one of them won.

كانت الشمس مرتفعة عندما شاهد سانتياجو طائرًا يغوص نحو البحر، مما دلّ على وجود الأسماك. وبعد قليل، شعر بسمكة قوية تبتلع الطُعم ببطء. ظل سانتياجو هادئًا وترك السمكة تبتلع الطُعم بالكامل قبل أن يشد الخيط. تعلقت السمكة العملاقة بالسنارة وبدأت تسحب القارب بعيدًا إلى عرض البحر. أُعجب سانتياجو بقوة السمكة ورفض الاستسلام. شرب قليلًا من الماء وأكل بعض التونة ليحافظ على قوته. ومع حلول الليل، استمرت السمكة في سحب القارب دون توقف. جرح خيط الصيد يديه وأصاب ظهره وذراعيه بالألم، لكنه ظل مصممًا على المواصلة. تذكر جو ديماجيو وشجع نفسه على تحمل الألم بشجاعة. تمنى لو كان مانولين معه ليساعده ويشهد هذه المعركة العظيمة. ورغم أنه كان وحيدًا تمامًا، شعر بأنه جزء من البحر والطبيعة. ومع شروق الفجر، كانت السمكة لا تزال قوية، وأدرك سانتياجو أن الصراع سيستمر حتى ينتصر أحدهما.

📖 The Text نص الفصل

0 / 0

The sun was high now, and the sea shone with a hard, bright light. Santiago wiped the sweat from his forehead and watched the bird circling. The old man knew that the bird was looking for fish near the surface. Suddenly, the bird dived straight down, and the water splashed. Small tuna jumped in the air, frightened by something larger below. Santiago's heart beat faster. He studied the lines with calm eyes, but inside he was excited. He had been waiting for this moment. His fingers felt the line tremble slightly. Then, without warning, the line began to move slowly, steadily.

Something powerful was taking the bait. The old man held the line carefully. He did not pull. He let the fish eat. He knew the ways of big fish. They circled, tested, and swallowed slowly.

Santiago whispered, "Take it, big one. Take it well."

Then the line tightened hard, cutting deep into his hand. The fish was hooked. Santiago braced his feet and leaned back. The line stretched out into the deep water with unstoppable force. The boat began to move slowly, pulled by the fish.

"He is strong," Santiago said aloud. "He will show me what strength is."

The fish did not jump. It swam steadily out into the open sea, far from all other boats. Santiago let it run, his hands steady though the line cut into his skin. He felt the power of the great creature below, pulling him farther and farther away from land. For hours, the fish swam on, and the boat followed. Santiago drank a little water and ate a piece of tuna he had caught earlier for bait. He needed strength, for this battle would not end quickly. As the sun went down, the line still pulled tight, and the fish still swam deep. The old man spoke to it softly:

"Fish, you are my brother. But I will not let you go. I will fight with all my heart to take you."

Night fell, and the stars came out. The boat moved quietly through the dark water. Santiago felt the line burning into his hands, but he held firm. His back ached, his arms trembled, but he would not surrender. He remembered Joe DiMaggio playing baseball with pain in his heel.

"If DiMaggio could play with pain, I can fight this fish," Santiago thought. "Pain does not matter. Only endurance matters."

The fish towed the boat all night. Santiago could not sleep. He tied the line across his shoulders to take some of the strain, but he never let go. He ate another piece of fish to keep his strength. Sometimes, he thought of the boy.

"I wish the boy were here," he whispered. "He would help me, and he would see what a great fish this is."

But Santiago was alone, and he knew this was his fight. The sea was silent except for the sound of water against the boat. The old man felt small under the wide sky, but also strong. He was part of the sea, part of the stars, part of the eternal struggle between man and nature. As dawn began to break again, Santiago looked at the line. It still cut hard into the water, strong and deep. The fish had not tired. The old man said aloud:

"Now we are joined, fish, you and I. You are pulling me, and I am pulling you. May the best of us win."

1Why does Santiago remember Joe DiMaggio during the struggle?

Because DiMaggio played baseball with a painful heel; his example gives Santiago courage to fight through his own pain.

2Why does Santiago call the fish his "brother"?

3How does the sea act as both a friend and an enemy in this chapter?
كيف يكون البحر صديقًا وعدوًا في هذا الفصل؟
It is a friend because it gives Santiago the great fish, food and a feeling of home; it is an enemy because it pulls him far from land and makes him suffer alone.
هو صديق لأنه يمنح سانتياجو السمكة الكبيرة والطعام وإحساس الوطن؛ وهو عدو لأنه يجره بعيدًا عن اليابسة ويجعله يعاني وحيدًا.
4Why does Santiago wish the boy were with him?
لماذا يتمنى سانتياجو أن يكون الصبي معه؟
Because he needs help with the line and food, and he wants someone to witness how great the fish is.
لأنه يحتاج إلى المساعدة في الخيط والطعام، ويريد شخصًا يشهد عظمة هذه السمكة.
5Why do you think Santiago continues even when conditions are difficult? أطسا ٢٠٢٦
لماذا يستمر سانتياجو حتى عندما تكون الظروف صعبة في رأيك؟
Because of his pride, determination and belief that a man is not made for defeat; giving up would mean losing his dignity.
بسبب كبريائه وعزيمته وإيمانه بأن الإنسان لم يُخلق للهزيمة؛ فالاستسلام يعني فقدان كرامته.
6Why does Hemingway describe Santiago as part of the sea and the stars?
لماذا يصف همنجواي سانتياجو بأنه جزء من البحر والنجوم؟
To show his deep harmony with nature; his struggle is part of the eternal struggle between man and nature, not a war against it.
ليُظهر انسجامه العميق مع الطبيعة؛ فصراعه جزء من الصراع الأبدي بين الإنسان والطبيعة، وليس حربًا ضدها.
7Do you think Santiago is fighting the fish, or is he fighting himself? Explain.

Both. He fights the fish physically, but he also fights his own age, pain, hunger and loneliness to prove that he is still strong.
كلاهما. فهو يحارب السمكة جسديًا، لكنه يحارب أيضًا شيخوخته وألمه وجوعه ووحدته ليثبت أنه لا يزال قويًا.

لأنه وحيد ويحتاج إلى الرفقة، ولأنه يحترم السمكة كخصم جدير وأخ.

📝 Summary ملخص الفصل

Santiago spent another day and night struggling with the giant marlin without sleeping. His hands were badly injured, and his body was exhausted, but he refused to give up. He admired the fish's strength and called it his brother, although he knew he had to kill it. To save his strength, he ate small pieces of raw tuna and drank a little water. He encouraged himself by remembering Joe DiMaggio's courage and endurance. The fish continued pulling the boat farther into the sea for two days. At last, the marlin jumped out of the water, and Santiago saw that it was larger than his boat. He was amazed by its beauty, size, and noble spirit. Although he respected and even loved the fish, he remained determined to defeat it. Santiago suffered greatly but believed that a man must work, struggle, and never surrender. By the third dawn, both the old man and the marlin were weak from the long battle. Santiago prayed for strength, knowing that only one of them could finally win.

قضى سانتياجو يومًا وليلة أخرى في صراع مع سمكة المارلين العملاقة دون أن ينام. كانت يداه مجروحتين بشدة، وكان جسده مرهقًا، لكنه رفض الاستسلام. أُعجب بقوة السمكة واعتبرها أخًا له، رغم أنه كان يعلم أنه يجب أن يقتلها. وللحفاظ على قوته، أكل قليلًا من سمك التونة النيء وشرب كمية قليلة من الماء. وشجع نفسه بتذكر شجاعة وتحمل جو ديماجيو. واستمرت السمكة في سحب القارب بعيدًا في البحر لمدة يومين. وأخيرًا، قفزت المارلين خارج الماء، فرأى سانتياجو أنها كانت أطول من قاربه. وانبهر بجمالها وضخامتها وروحها النبيلة. ورغم احترامه وحبه لها، ظل مصممًا على هزيمتها. وتحمل سانتياجو آلامًا شديدة، لكنه كان يؤمن بأن الإنسان خُلق ليعمل ويكافح ولا يستسلم. ومع فجر اليوم الثالث، كان كل من سانتياجو والسمكة قد أنهكهما الصراع الطويل. فدعا الله أن يمنحهما القوة، وهو يعلم أن أحدهما فقط سيكون المنتصر.

📖 The Text نص الفصل

0 / 0

The morning sun rose golden over the sea, and the sky turned from black to pale blue. Santiago had not slept. His body was stiff, his hands were cut from the line, and his back ached from leaning against the pull of the great fish. Yet his eyes were clear, and his spirit unbroken. The fish still swam powerfully, dragging the boat farther out into the gulf. Santiago knew they were alone now, far from other fishermen, far from the coast. But he did not feel fear. Instead, he felt pride.

"No one will see this fight," he said aloud, "but I will know it, and so will the fish."

He looked at the line, stretched tight into the water.

"You are my brother, fish," he whispered, "but I must kill you. There is no other way."

To rest his hands, Santiago shifted the line across his shoulders, letting the rough hemp bite into his back instead of his palms. He breathed deeply and ate another piece of tuna, chewing slowly. He knew he must save his strength. The battle was not about hours, but days. By noon, the fish suddenly pulled harder, and Santiago braced himself. The line cut deeper into his skin, but he did not let go. His teeth clenched, sweat poured down his face. For a moment, he thought the fish might leap, but it did not.

Instead, it dove deeper, dragging the skiff slowly along. The old man admired the creature's power.

"He has not shown himself yet," he thought. "He is too wise. But soon, he must come up."

The hours passed. The sun burned hot, and Santiago shaded his eyes. His muscles cramped, but he stretched them against the pain. He thought again of Joe DiMaggio, who played baseball with a bone spur in his heel.

"If he could play with pain, I can fight with pain," Santiago repeated. "I am only an old man, but I can endure."

That night, the fish made a great move. It surged suddenly, pulling the boat faster than ever. Santiago almost fell, but he held on, his body trembling with the effort. His hands bled freely, but he ignored the pain.

"You are killing me, fish," he said aloud, "but you have the right. Never have I seen such a strong one. But I will not give in."

When the stars came out again, Santiago felt both loneliness and companionship. He was alone on the sea, but the fish was with him, bound by the line between them. He looked up at the stars and remembered the lions of his youth, playing on the beaches of Africa. That dream gave him strength. The next morning, the fish finally rose.

Santiago saw the line move up, felt the great force lifting. Then, in a sudden explosion, the marlin leapt high into the air. It was enormous — longer than the boat itself, silver in the sunlight, shining like a living sword. Water cascaded from its body as it crashed back into the sea. Santiago's heart jumped.

"Never have I seen such a fish," he whispered in awe. "Noble, strong, and full of spirit."

The marlin dived again, and the struggle continued. But now Santiago knew the size of his enemy. He spoke softly:

"You are the greatest fish I have ever fought. I will kill you, though it will take all my strength."

For two days and two nights, the battle continued. Santiago did not sleep. He ate little, only raw fish, and drank sparingly from his water bottle. His body was broken, but his will was like iron. At times he pitied the fish.

"You are killing yourself for me," he said. "I love you, but I must take you. A man was born to work, to fight, to suffer, and to win."

When the third dawn came, Santiago was near exhaustion. His eyes burned, his hands were raw, his back felt as if it would break. Yet the line still held tight. The marlin swam slower now, tired but still strong. Santiago whispered to the sea, to the fish, to himself:

"It is you or me. May God help us both."

ماذا يقصد سانتياجو بقوله «إما أنت أو أنا»؟
He means the battle is a fight for survival: either he will catch the fish, or the fish will destroy him; only one of them can win.
يقصد أن المعركة صراع من أجل البقاء: إما أن يصطاد السمكة أو تقضي هي عليه؛ فواحد منهما فقط سينتصر.
2Why does Hemingway show Santiago speaking to the fish as if it were human?
لماذا يُظهر همنجواي سانتياجو وهو يتحدث إلى السمكة كأنها إنسان؟
To show Santiago's loneliness and his deep respect for the fish as a brother and a noble opponent, and to make the struggle feel personal.
ليُظهر وحدة سانتياجو واحترامه العميق للسمكة كأخ وخصم نبيل، وليجعل الصراع يبدو شخصيًا.
3What role do Santiago's memories of the lions play in his struggle?
ما دور ذكريات سانتياجو عن الأسود في صراعه؟
The lions remind him of his youth, strength and courage; the dream gives him hope and energy to keep fighting.
تذكّره الأسود بشبابه وقوته وشجاعته؛ فالحلم يمنحه الأمل والطاقة لمواصلة القتال.
4Why does Santiago compare himself to Joe DiMaggio?
لماذا يقارن سانتياجو نفسه بجو ديماجيو؟
Because DiMaggio played baseball with a painful bone spur in his heel; if a hero can play with pain, Santiago can fight with pain too.
لأن ديماجيو كان يلعب البيسبول رغم نتوء عظمي مؤلم في كعبه؛ فإذا كان البطل يلعب رغم الألم، فسانتياجو يستطيع أن يقاتل رغم الألم أيضًا.
5Why does Santiago admire the marlin even while trying to kill it?
لماذا يُعجب سانتياجو بالمارلين رغم محاولته قتلها؟
Because it is huge, beautiful, strong and noble; it fights bravely without giving up, just like Santiago himself.
لأنها ضخمة وجميلة وقوية ونبيلة؛ تقاتل بشجاعة دون استسلام، تمامًا مثل سانتياجو نفسه.
6How does Santiago's endurance highlight the theme of human resilience?
كيف يبرز تحمل سانتياجو فكرة صمود الإنسان؟
Despite hunger, bleeding hands, cramps and no sleep for days, he keeps holding the line; this shows that the human spirit can endure far beyond the body's limits.
رغم الجوع ويديه النازفتين والتشنجات وعدم النوم لأيام، يظل ممسكًا بالخيط؛ وهذا يبين أن روح الإنسان قادرة على التحمل أبعد بكثير من حدود الجسد.
7What does shifting the line across his shoulders show about Santiago's endurance?
ماذا يُظهر نقل الخيط إلى كتفيه عن تحمل سانتياجو؟
It shows his wisdom and experience; he uses his whole body to share the pain so that he can hold on for days without letting go.
يُظهر حكمته وخبرته؛ فهو يستخدم جسده كله لتوزيع الألم حتى يتمكن من الصمود لأيام دون أن يترك الخيط.
8What role do Santiago's memories of the lions play in his struggle?
ما دور ذكريات الأسود في صراع سانتياجو؟
They are a source of inner strength; the lions symbolize the courage and youth that still live inside the old man.
إنها مصدر للقوة الداخلية؛ فالأسود ترمز إلى الشجاعة والشباب اللذين لا يزالان يعيشان داخل الرجل العجوز.
9What does the marlin's leap symbolize in the story?
ماذا يرمز قفز المارلين في القصة؟
It symbolizes the greatness and pride of nature; the fish shows its full power and beauty, making the struggle a fight between two noble spirits.
يرمز إلى عظمة الطبيعة وكبريائها؛ فالسمكة تُظهر كامل قوتها وجمالها، مما يجعل الصراع معركة بين روحين نبيلتين.
10Do you agree with Santiago that "a man was born to work, to fight, to suffer, and to win"? Why or why not?
هل توافق سانتياجو على أن «الإنسان وُلد ليعمل ويكافح ويعاني وينتصر»؟ ولماذا؟
Yes, I agree. Life is full of challenges, and real success comes only through hard work, patience and suffering; those who never give up are the true winners.
نعم أوافق. فالحياة مليئة بالتحديات، والنجاح الحقيقي لا يأتي إلا بالعمل الجاد والصبر والمعاناة؛ ومن لا يستسلم هو المنتصر الحقيقي.

The Great Marlin Revealed

📝 Summary ملخص الفصل

After three days and nights, Santiago realized that the marlin was finally becoming weaker. He patiently pulled the line until the giant fish came close to the surface. The marlin was enormous, beautiful, and full of strength, which filled Santiago with admiration and respect. When the right moment came, Santiago used his harpoon and killed the fish with one powerful strike. Although he was proud of his victory, he also felt sad because he had killed such a noble creature. He tied the huge marlin beside his small boat and started the journey back home. Santiago hoped that everyone would believe his achievement and that Manolin would be proud of him. However, he knew that the smell of the fish's blood would attract sharks. He decided to fight them to protect his valuable catch. That night, he felt both happiness and sadness while thinking about the hard battle. He dreamed of the lions of his youth, which always gave him hope and strength. The old man continued sailing toward home, ready to face whatever challenges awaited him.

بعد ثلاثة أيام وثلاث ليالٍ، أدرك سانتياجو أن سمكة المارلين بدأت تضعف أخيرًا. سحب الخيط بصبر حتى اقتربت السمكة العملاقة من سطح الماء. كانت السمكة ضخمة وجميلة ومليئة بالقوة، مما جعله يشعر بالإعجاب والاحترام تجاهها. وعندما جاءت اللحظة المناسبة، استخدم سانتياجو الحربة وقتل السمكة بضربة قوية. ورغم فخره بانتصاره، شعر بالحزن لأنه قتل مخلوقًا نبيلًا. ربط المارلين الضخم بجانب قاربه الصغير وبدأ رحلة العودة إلى الوطن. كان يأمل أن يصدق الجميع إنجازه وأن يشعر مانولين بالفخر به. لكنه كان يعلم أن رائحة دم السمكة ستجذب أسماك القرش، لذلك قرر أن يقاتلها لحماية صيده الثمين. وفي تلك الليلة، شعر بالسعادة والحزن في الوقت نفسه وهو يتذكر المعركة الشاقة. وحلم بأسود شبابه التي كانت دائمًا تمنحه الأمل والقوة. واستمر الرجل العجوز في الإبحار نحو منزله، مستعدًا لمواجهة أي تحديات تنتظره.

📖 The Text نص الفصل

0 / 0

The sun was rising again. Santiago had been fighting the fish for three long days and nights. His body was weary, his hands swollen and bleeding, but his spirit remained sharp. He knew the fish was weakening, though its strength was still greater than anything he had ever faced. The line pulled with less power now, and Santiago felt the fish circling slowly deep below the boat. He recognized the pattern: the marlin was tired, but it would not surrender easily. It was preparing for its final struggle.

"Now it begins," the old man whispered.

He braced his feet against the wooden boards of the skiff and leaned back with all the strength left in him. The fish circled wider and wider. Each turn brought it a little closer to the surface. Santiago worked carefully, pulling in the line inch by inch. His muscles burned, but he welcomed the pain.

"Pain is not an enemy," he thought. "It tells me I am alive."

At last, the marlin rose. The giant fish came into view, silver and purple in the water, glowing in the sunlight. Santiago gasped at its size. It was longer than the boat, with a great sword-like bill and a powerful body. The marlin swam gracefully, a king of the sea.

"Fish," Santiago said aloud, his voice full of respect, "you are my brother, but I must end this. Forgive me."

With trembling hands, he prepared his harpoon. He knew this moment would decide everything. The fish surfaced again, circling near the boat, its dorsal fin cutting the water. Santiago gathered his strength, lifted the harpoon high, and when the fish came close, he drove the iron deep into its heart. The marlin leapt, shining in the air one last time, then crashed into the sea with a thunderous splash. Its body shook, the water boiled, and then it was still. The great fish floated beside the boat, slowly turning on its side, its silver scales catching the sun. Santiago dropped the harpoon and leaned against the mast, shaking with exhaustion and triumph. Tears filled his eyes, not only from victory but from sorrow.

"I have killed the most noble of creatures," he whispered. "He did not deserve to die, but I needed to live."

With careful hands, the old man tied the marlin to the side of his skiff. Its body was so large that it stretched far beyond the boat's length. The fish was heavy, majestic, a prize greater than anything Santiago had ever caught. For a moment, he allowed himself to feel pride.

"They will not believe me," he thought. "They will say no man could take such a fish alone. But I know. And the boy will know. That is enough."

The boat began its long journey home. Santiago's arms were weak, but the wind carried him gently toward the coast. He looked at the marlin's shining body in the water.

"We fought well, fish," he said softly. "You gave me everything you had. And I gave you everything I had. This was fair."

The sea was calm, the sun warm. Santiago felt at peace, though he knew his work was not finished. The hardest part was yet to come: bringing his prize safely home. As the boat sailed, Santiago dreamed of how the villagers would react. The fishermen would measure the marlin, and the boy would be proud. People would see that the old man was not finished, that he was still strong, still capable of greatness. But Santiago also knew that victory carried danger. The smell of blood in the water would call the sharks. He looked at the horizon, his eyes hard.

"They will come," he said. "But I will fight them."

The marlin floated beside him, silent, beautiful, and dead. The old man placed his hand gently on the fish's side.

"We are joined forever, you and I," he whispered. "Your death gives me life, but it costs me my soul."

Night fell once more, and Santiago, though exhausted, kept watch. He felt both proud and deeply sad. He had won the greatest battle of his life, but he sensed that the sea would test him again before he reached home. He closed his eyes briefly, and in his half-dream, he saw the lions of his youth on the African shore, running and playing freely. They gave him strength, as they always did. When he opened his eyes, he looked again at the marlin, shining in the moonlight.

"Tomorrow, we will face what comes," he said. "For now, we rest together."

The boat sailed on into the darkness, carrying the old man and his mighty prize toward an uncertain dawn.

Because he still has to bring the fish safely home, and he knows the sharks will come to attack it.

8How does Santiago show respect for the marlin even as he kills it?
كيف يُظهر سانتياجو احترامه للمارلين حتى وهو يقتلها؟

يناديها بأخيه، ويطلب منها المسامحة، ويقول إن المعركة كانت عادلة، ويضع يده برفق على جانبها.
9Why does Hemingway describe the marlin as majestic and noble?

To show that Santiago's opponent is worthy and great; defeating such a fish makes his achievement truly heroic.

📝 Summary ملخص الفصل

As Santiago sailed home, the giant marlin was tied to his boat, shining in the light. Though proud, Santiago felt uneasy, knowing the scent of blood would attract sharks. A fierce mako shark attacked first, and Santiago killed it with his harpoon, but the marlin lost a chunk of flesh. Soon, more sharks arrived. Santiago fought bravely, even after his harpoon broke — using a knife tied to an oar, then even broken pieces of wood as weapons. Despite his efforts, the sharks devoured most of the marlin, leaving only its skeleton. At night, utterly exhausted, Santiago said to the stars: "I fought for the marlin as long as I could. He was too noble to be lost without a fight." When the sea finally grew quiet, Santiago looked at the glowing white skeleton and said sadly: "You were my greatest enemy and my greatest friend. They destroyed you, but not my pride." Thinking of Manolin, he smiled faintly, believing the boy would help him tomorrow. The small boat sailed silently toward shore, carrying a broken old man, an unbroken spirit, and a skeleton that told a tale of both victory and tragedy.

بينما كان سانتياجو عائدًا إلى الشاطئ، كان المارلين العملاق مربوطًا إلى القارب، يلمع تحت ضوء الشمس. شعر بالفخر، لكن القلق تملكه لأن رائحة الدم ستجذب أسماك القرش. ظهر أول قرش، سريعًا وقويًا، فواجهه سانتياجو بكل ما تبقى له من قوة وقتله، لكن السمكة فقدت جزءًا من لحمها. سرعان ما تبعت القرش الأول مجموعة أخرى، فقاتلهم سانتياجو واحدًا تلو الآخر. كُسر رمحه، فربط سكينًا بمجداف ليستخدمه كسلاح، وظل يقاتل حتى تفتت المجداف نفسه. رغم قتله لبعض القروش، استمرت المعركة حتى أكلت القروش معظم جسد المارلين، ولم يتبقَّ سوى هيكله العظمي. في الليل، كان سانتياجو منهكًا، لكنه لم يستسلم. قال للنجوم: «لقد قاتلت من أجل هذه السمكة حتى النهاية، لأنها كانت نبيلة جدًا لتُفقد بلا صراع». عندما حل الهدوء أخيرًا، نظر إلى الهيكل الأبيض اللامع في ضوء القمر وقال بحزن: «لقد كنتَ أعظم أعدائي وأعظم أصدقائي. لقد دمّروك، لكنهم لم يمسّوا كبريائي». ثم تذكر الصبي مانولين وابتسم بخفة، مؤمنًا أنه لن يتركه وحيدًا. أبحر القارب بهدوء نحو الشاطئ، حاملًا صيادًا عجوزًا وروحًا لا تزال قوية، وهيكلًا يروي قصة انتصار ممزوج بالمأساة.

📖 The Text نص الفصل

0 / 0

The morning sun rose as Santiago's small skiff sailed steadily toward the shore. The giant marlin was tied beside the boat, its silver body shining in the light. Santiago, though proud, felt uneasy. The sea was never generous without asking for something in return. He knew the scent of blood would call predators. And then he saw it: a dark shadow moving swiftly beneath the surface. A shark. It was a mako shark, fast and strong, following the marlin's trail of blood. Santiago's heart tightened.

"So, it begins," he muttered.

He took up his harpoon, though his hands were raw and shaking. The shark came closer, its sharp teeth glinting as it attacked the marlin's side. With all the strength left in him, Santiago drove the harpoon down into the shark's head. The iron struck deep, and the shark thrashed violently, turning the sea red. Finally, it sank, dead, into the depths. But the victory was bitter. The marlin had lost a great piece of flesh, and blood flowed freely from its wound. Santiago looked at his catch with sorrow.

"They will come now, one after another," he said.

He was right. Before long, more shadows appeared. A pair of galanos — shovel-nosed sharks — rose from the deep. They were slower but insistent. They bit at the marlin, tearing away its flesh. Santiago fought with his harpoon until it broke off in a shark's body. Now, he tied his knife to an oar and used it as a spear. He stabbed and slashed, killing one shark and driving the other away. But each battle cost him strength, and the marlin's body grew smaller, its beauty ruined. As the hours passed, more sharks came. The smell of blood had spread far through the sea. Santiago fought them all, his arms burning, his vision blurring. He killed several but knew he could not stop them forever.

By afternoon, the marlin was only half a fish. Its head and backbone remained, but much of its flesh was gone. Santiago leaned against the mast, breathing heavily.

"I was beaten," he whispered, "but only by sharks, not by the fish."

Still, he did not surrender. Every time a new shark attacked, he stood up and fought. He swung the oar-spear until it splintered, then used the tiller, then even the broken pieces of wood. He was an old man with nothing left but his will. Night fell again, and Santiago was exhausted beyond words. The marlin was now only a skeleton, stripped of nearly all its meat.

But Santiago kept sailing toward home, his spirit unbroken.

"I fought for the marlin as long as I could," he said aloud to the stars. "He was too noble to be lost without a fight."

At last, silence returned. No more sharks came. The marlin's skeleton glowed white in the moonlight, its long sword rising like a banner of both triumph and tragedy. Santiago looked at it and felt tears in his eyes.

"You were my greatest enemy and my greatest friend," he told the fish. "They destroyed you, but they could not destroy my pride. We fought well."

He thought of the boy, and a faint smile touched his lips.

"The boy will not let me be alone again," he said. "Tomorrow, he will help me. He must."

Santiago steered the little skiff through the dark waters, his body broken but his spirit still alive. He had lost his catch, but he had not lost his dignity. The sea was quiet again, carrying the old man and the skeleton of the marlin slowly toward the shore.

❓ Setbook Questions & Answers أسئلة كتاب المدرسة

1Why does Santiago call the first shark attack "the beginning"?
لماذا يسمي سانتياجو هجوم القرش الأول «البداية»؟
Because it starts a new struggle after catching the marlin.
لأنه يبدأ صراعًا جديدًا بعد صيد المارلين.
2How does Santiago show courage when facing the mako shark?
كيف يظهر سانتياجو الشجاعة عند مواجهة قرش الماكو؟
He fights it with his harpoon despite danger.
يصارع القرش بحربته رغم الخطر.
3What does the breaking of the harpoon symbolize?
ماذا يرمز كسر الرمح؟
It shows that tools fail, but the struggle continues.
يظهر أن الأدوات قد تفشل، لكن الصراع يستمر.
4Why does Santiago keep fighting even when the marlin is nearly gone?
لماذا يستمر سانتياجو في القتال رغم أن المارلين كانت على وشك الانتهاء؟
He wants to protect his catch and maintain pride.
يريد حماية صيده والحفاظ على كبريائه.
5How do the galanos differ from the mako shark?
كيف تختلف أسماك الجالانو عن قرش الماكو؟
They are smaller but attack in groups and are persistent.
هم أصغر لكنهم يهاجمون في جماعات ويثابرون.
6What does Santiago mean when he says he was beaten by sharks, not the fish?
ماذا يعني سانتياجو عندما يقول إنه هُزم بواسطة أسماك القرش، وليس السمكة؟
The marlin fought nobly, but the sharks destroyed it.
صار المارلين شريفًا في قتاله، لكن أسماك القرش دمرته.
7How does Santiago's hope in the boy give meaning to his suffering?
كيف يعطي أمل سانتياجو في الصبي معنى لمعاناته؟
Thinking of the boy gives him strength and motivation to continue.
التفكير في الصبي يمنحه القوة والدافع للاستمرار.

1Why does Santiago still call the marlin his "greatest friend" even after its death?

Heroic, because he never gave up despite impossible odds.
بطولي، لأنه لم يستسلم أبدًا رغم صعوبة الوضع.

✍️ General Exercises تدريبات عامة (مع إجابات نموذجية)

1Do you think Santiago is a hero? Why or why not? الهرم ٢٠٢٦
هل تعتقد أن سانتياجو بطل؟ ولماذا؟
Yes. A hero is not someone who never loses, but someone who never gives up. Santiago fought the marlin for three days and then the sharks with broken tools, and he kept his dignity to the end.
نعم. فالبطل ليس من لا يخسر أبدًا، بل من لا يستسلم أبدًا. قاتل سانتياجو المارلين ثلاثة أيام ثم القروش بأدوات مكسورة، وحافظ على كرامته حتى النهاية.
2What lesson do you think Santiago learns from his struggle with the marlin and the sharks? أطسا ٢٠٢٦
ما الدرس الذي تعلمه سانتياجو من صراعه مع المارلين والقروش في رأيك؟
He learns that a man can be destroyed but not defeated; what matters is how bravely you fight, not what you bring home.
يتعلم أن الإنسان قد يُدمَّر لكنه لا يُهزم؛ فالمهم هو مدى شجاعتك في القتال، لا ما تعود به إلى البيت.
3What message does this chapter send about pride and loss?
ما الرسالة التي يرسلها هذا الفصل عن الكبرياء والخسارة؟
We may lose the things we fight for, but we can keep our pride and honor if we fight well.
قد نخسر الأشياء التي نقاتل من أجلها، لكن يمكننا أن نحتفظ بكبريائنا وشرفنا إذا قاتلنا جيدًا.
4Why does Hemingway describe the sharks coming "one after another"?
لماذا يصف همنجواي القروش بأنها تأتي «واحدًا تلو الآخر»؟
To show that troubles in life do not stop; each victory brings a new test, and endurance is needed again and again.
ليبين أن متاعب الحياة لا تتوقف؛ فكل انتصار يجلب اختبارًا جديدًا، والتحمل مطلوب مرة بعد مرة.
5What role does dignity play in Santiago's battle with the sharks?
ما دور الكرامة في معركة سانتياجو مع القروش؟
Dignity is the reason he keeps fighting even when the fish is nearly gone; he refuses to let the marlin be eaten without a fight.
الكرامة هي سبب استمراره في القتال حتى عندما تكاد السمكة تختفي؛ فهو يرفض أن تُؤكل المارلين دون قتال.
6How is the marlin both a victory and a tragedy in this chapter?
كيف تكون المارلين انتصارًا ومأساة في هذا الفصل؟
It is a victory because Santiago caught the greatest fish of his life; it is a tragedy because the sharks destroyed it and left only a skeleton.
هي انتصار لأن سانتياجو اصطاد أعظم سمكة في حياته؛ وهي مأساة لأن القروش دمرتها ولم تترك سوى هيكل عظمي.
7Why does Santiago view the marlin as both a brother and an enemy? المنشأة ٢٠٢٦
لماذا يرى سانتياجو المارلين أخًا وعدوًا؟
It was his enemy in the battle, but its courage and nobility made him love and respect it like a brother.
كانت عدوه في المعركة، لكن شجاعتها ونبلها جعلاه يحبها ويحترمها كأخ.
8In what way is Santiago's battle with sharks different from his battle with the marlin?
كيف تختلف معركة سانتياجو مع القروش عن معركته مع المارلين؟
The battle with the marlin was a fair fight between two noble opponents; the battle with the sharks was a hopeless fight against greedy destroyers with broken weapons.
كانت معركة المارلين قتالًا عادلًا بين خصمين نبيلين؛ أما معركة القروش فكانت قتالًا يائسًا ضد مدمرين جشعين بأسلحة مكسورة.
9How does Santiago's refusal to surrender show the theme of human dignity?
كيف يُظهر رفض سانتياجو للاستسلام موضوع الكرامة الإنسانية؟
It shows that dignity comes from the way we face hardship; even with nothing left but his will, he stands and fights.
يُظهر أن الكرامة تأتي من طريقة مواجهتنا للشدائد؛ فحتى وهو لا يملك سوى إرادته، يقف ويقاتل.
10Why does Hemingway describe Santiago using even broken pieces of wood to fight?
لماذا يصف همنجواي سانتياجو وهو يقاتل حتى بقطع الخشب المكسورة؟
To show that he is weaponless but not powerless; his will to fight is stronger than any tool.
ليبين أنه بلا سلاح لكن ليس بلا قوة؛ فإرادته في القتال أقوى من أي أداة.
